title: how_ai_changes_agency_retainers
claim: AI reduces the cost of creative execution to zero, forcing marketing budgets to shift entirely from paying for production volume to paying for strategic judgment.
hook: How AI is changing marketing isn't by replacing creative work, but by making generic execution cost zero.

reel_script.voiceover: How AI is changing marketing isn't by replacing your job. It is by making generic execution cost zero.
reel_script.direction: Rachit speaking directly to camera, sitting at desk.

reel_script.voiceover: For twenty years, agency retainers bought asset volume: ten ad variations, five emails, twenty social graphics.
AI tools generate those variations in three seconds. If your team is still billing for execution hours, you are paying a tax on slow software.
When production cost drops to zero, content volume increases tenfold. But consumer attention stays exactly the same.
The bottleneck isn't production anymore. It is filter strength. AI generates a hundred taglines, but cannot choose which operational trade-off your brand will stand behind.
Stop evaluating agency scopes by deliverable count. Start paying for the bad positioning decisions they prevent you from making.

reel_script.onscreen: Send this to your brand lead.
reel_script.voiceover: Send this to your brand manager or agency partner before your next scope review.

caption:
How AI is changing marketing isn't by replacing creative work, but by making generic execution cost zero.

Historically, brand retainers were priced on deliverable volume: 15 ad variations, 4 email sequences, 20 social banners. Generative tools now produce that baseline output in seconds.

When production costs collapse, flooding channels with mid-tier assets creates noise, not market share. The constraint shifts from how fast your team can execute to how sharply your team can filter.

An algorithm can produce fifty campaign hooks, but it cannot decide which customer segment your positioning explicitly sacrifices.

AI doesn't eliminate marketers; it eliminates the leverage of charging human hours for mechanical execution.

Send this to your brand manager or agency lead before setting your next scope of work.
